questions.q: For a gas-phase reaction at constant T and P, express C_A in terms of conversion and ε.
questions.m: C_A = C_A0 (1 − X)/(1 + εX), where ε = y_A0 δ and δ is the change in total moles per mole of A reacted. The volumetric flow rate varies as v = v₀(1 + εX) for isothermal, isobaric operation.

questions.q: Explain thermal runaway and multiple steady states in a CSTR using G(T) and R(T) curves.
questions.m: Heat generation G(T) is sigmoidal in T (Arrhenius at low T and saturating at high T when conversion approaches 1); heat removal R(T) is roughly linear. Intersections are steady states: low-temperature, middle (unstable) and high-temperature (stable) points can all exist. A small disturbance or an increase in feed temperature can push the system across the unstable point so the temperature 'ignites' to the high-T steady state (runaway); a design must keep R(T) slope and cooling capacity adequate to avoid this.

questions.q: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by:
c: Providing a pathway with lower activation energy without altering the equilibrium constant
questions.e: It accelerates forward and reverse reactions equally.

questions.q: The Langmuir adsorption isotherm gives surface coverage:
What does the Thiele modulus describe and what does η → 1 mean?
questions.m: The Thiele modulus φ compares the intrinsic surface reaction rate to the rate of internal diffusion in a catalyst pellet (φ² ∝ k L²/D_e). The effectiveness factor η is the actual rate divided by the rate with no diffusion limitation. For small φ, η → 1: the pellet is entirely accessible and the reaction is kinetically controlled; for large φ, η ≈ 1/φ and internal diffusion limits the rate.
